reason: The cited evidence describes a modified process and a multi-scale structure (E3) and links room-temperature ductility to high-temperature life (E2), but it does not provide specific prior evidence that the process induces high dislocation density and fine MC carbides, nor that these specific mechanisms govern high-temperature strain and toughness. The mechanistic claims are largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: A modified thermomechanical process induces high dislocation density and fine MC carbides in RAFM steel.
High dislocation density and fine MC carbides combine work hardening, precipitation hardening, and grain boundary strengthening.
This combination of strengthening mechanisms improves high-temperature plastic strain and toughness.
Improved room temperature elongation extends high-temperature service life and irradiation resistance.
A multi-scale ferrite/martensite structure extends uniform elongation without over-reliance on strain hardening.
